reason: Compared the complete source def:crossings and inherited cyclic-representative conventions with the compiled aggregate SM.crossingData and all supporting definitions and properties. The aggregate includes the actual crossing set, common point, on-edge parameter and directed crossing sign, and the audited semantic dependencies bind every defining component. IsCrossing requires a support equal to an unordered pair of remote modular indices whose actual closed affine edge segments have nonempty intersection. crossingSet is precisely the finite set of those supports, by mem_crossingSet, and crossing_card_two shows that remoteness forces exactly two indices. The Crossing subtype adds only this geometric membership proof, not an ordering or distinguished edge. crossingPoint is chosen from a proved existence of a point on both constituent segments; crossingPoint_mem supplies membership, and crossingPoint_unique identifies it with the unique geometric intersection on the source G1 domain. crossingPoint_interior and crossingParameter_interior supply strict interior membership and 0<t<1. crossingParameter_spec gives exactly x=P i+t*(P(i+1)-P i), so each chosen parameter is the source parameter on its specified tail-indexed edge. Parameter uniqueness follows from the proved injectivity of edgePoint when that edge is nonzero, which G1 establishes for n>=3. This prevents Classical.choose from supplying arbitrary values unrelated to the geometry. crossingSign P i j is sign(det(edge P i,edge P j)), with the first index denoting the edge from which the crossing is read, and crossingSign_swap gives the expected reversal. Raw definitions are extended beyond G1, but uniqueness and interiority are proved under precisely G1 and the inherited n>=3 domain; no source case is discarded or extra hypothesis required. The added crossingShiftEquiv is an actual equivalence between crossings of P and shift a P: its forward support translation sends an old index i to i-a, and its explicit inverse sends the shifted index back by adding a. Both inverse identities are proved. This direction matches shift a P at index i being P(i+a). crossingPoint_shift preserves the actual geometric point, crossingParameter_shift preserves each parameter on its translated index, and crossingSign_shift preserves the directed determinant sign. Together with mem_crossingSet these prove cyclic equivariance of the complete crossing construction. The source expressly allows labelled representatives with these relabelling laws, so no arbitrary fixed-label structure is imposed on the polygon quotient. All definition clauses and the representative convention are accounted for. The former missing equivariance obligation is resolved; none of the supporting helper results is counted as an additional original source claim. The seven previously reviewed supporting files were verified byte-for-byte unchanged, and the final eighth file was inspected including the explicit finite-support inverse proof.

countersignature_20260913.reason: Source (reference/SM/sm-1-polygons.tex:138-146, byte-identical to the blueprint extract; not in the SM15 change table, sm15_reworded=false) defines, for P satisfying (G1): X(P) = unordered pairs {i,j} of remote edge indices with E_i ∩ E_j ≠ ∅; x_ij = the unique point of E_i ∩ E_j; parameters t_ij, t_ji ∈ (0,1) with x_ij = μ_i + t_ij λ_i = μ_j + t_ji λ_j; crossing sign read from E_i = sgn det(λ_i, λ_j). Lean (work/lean/SM/Crossings.lean:12-19, 41-42, 70-72, 80-81; aggregate SM.crossingData at CrossingEquiv.lean:79-80): IsCrossing P s := ∃ i j, s = {i,j} ∧ remote i j ∧ (edgeSegment P i ∩ edgeSegment P j).Nonempty, with remote := ¬(j−i ∈ {−1,0,1}) (Polygon.lean:63-66) exactly the printed adjacency/remoteness, edgeSegment P i = {μ_i + t λ_i : 0 ≤ t ≤ 1} (Polygon.lean:49-55), so crossingSet P = filter IsCrossing over all finsets is X(P) as a set of 2-element finsets (remote forces i ≠ j; crossing_card_two). crossingPoint c is a chosen common point of both segments; crossingPoint_unique (Crossings.lean:61-63) proves under G1 that any common point equals it, so on the printed domain it denotes the unique point x_ij; crossingPoint_interior gives relative-interior membership. crossingParameter c i hi is a t with 0 ≤ t ≤ 1 and crossingPoint c = P i + t • (P(i+1) − P i) (crossingParameter_spec, Crossings.lean:74-78), i.e. x_ij = μ_i + t_ij λ_i on edge i (and likewise for j), unique because edge P i ≠ 0 under G1 (edgePoint_injective, g1_edge_ne_zero) and strictly in (0,1) under 3 ≤ n and G1 (crossingParameter_interior, Crossings.lean:102-104). crossingSign P i j = SignType.sign (det (edge P i) (edge P j)) with det u v = u.1*v.2 − u.2*v.1 (Polygon.lean:16) is sgn det(λ_i, λ_j) read from E_i. G1 (Generic.lean:11-12) and chi (Chirotope.lean:10-11) match def:generic (G1) and def:chirotope. Working on labelled tuples with shift-equivariance recorded (crossingShiftEquiv, crossingPoint_shift, crossingParameter_shift, crossingSign_shift; shift 1 = σ since (shift a P) i = P(i+a)) is expressly permitted by the source's formalization remark. Nothing is vacuous: the definitions have the intended content for every n ≥ 3, and for n ≤ 3 the crossing set is correctly empty. All eight reviewed Lean files hash-match the accepted review; no sorry/axiom. My independent judgement agrees with the existing review.
stronger_than_source: The Lean crossing set, point, parameter and sign are total definitions on every LabelledTuple n (only [NeZero n] for crossingSet/crossingData), not restricted to P satisfying (G1) or to n ≥ 3; on the printed domain (G1, n ≥ 3) the uniqueness/interiority theorems show they coincide with the printed objects, and off it the source defines nothing, so this is a harmless generalization (crossingPoint is then merely some common point).
crossingSign P i j is defined for every ordered pair (i, j), not only for pairs in X(P); on crossings it is exactly the printed 'sign read from E_i'.

Shift-equivariance of all four components is stated explicitly (crossingShiftEquiv, crossingPoint_shift, crossingParameter_shift, crossingSign_shift), which the source only asserts in prose ('invariant under σ up to relabelling').
